differences.title: 1. REACTIVITY GRANULARITY
differences.leftDesc: SolidJS tracks dependencies at the expression level: when a signal changes, only computations that read it re-run, updating their owning DOM nodes directly without walking an entire component tree.
differences.rightDesc: React tracks changes at the component level: state updates schedule a render pass, and React reconciles the returned element tree to determine which subtree updates, potentially re-rendering many components.

differences.title: 2. RENDERING MECHANISM
differences.leftDesc: Solid compiles JSX into reactive primitives that create DOM once, then uses reactive effects to update text/attributes in place. There’s no incremental virtual DOM diff step during updates.
differences.rightDesc: React uses a virtual representation (JSX -> elements) and reconciliation to compare previous and next children. Updates compute which DOM mutations are needed based on diffed element structure.

differences.title: 3. CHANGE PROPAGATION
differences.leftDesc: When you set a signal, Solid propagates changes through its dependency graph, executing affected computations immediately in deterministic order, unless explicitly deferred via transitions or async patterns.
differences.rightDesc: React may batch multiple state updates and uses a scheduling model. With concurrent features, updates can be interrupted, deferred, or coalesced before committing to the DOM.

differences.title: 4. COMPONENT RE-EXECUTION
differences.leftDesc: In Solid, function components typically execute once to set up reactive computations; afterward, only dependent computations re-run. This avoids repeated component execution for unrelated state changes.
differences.rightDesc: With React hooks, a component function is re-executed whenever its state/props change for that render. Even if the UI change is localized, the component body runs to produce new elements.

differences.title: 5. MEMOIZATION NEEDS
differences.leftDesc: Because updates are expression-targeted, Solid often avoids heavy memoization wrappers for correctness. You still use memos for expensive computations, but they’re usually fewer in count.
differences.rightDesc: React frequently needs memoization/optimization to prevent unnecessary re-renders: useMemo/useCallback, React.memo, and stable props. Correctness is fine without them, but performance depends on patterns.

differences.title: 6. DERIVED STATE MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Solid provides computed derivations that subscribe to the exact signals they read. Derived values update only when their true dependencies change, minimizing wasted work.
differences.rightDesc: React derived values are commonly computed during render from state/props, meaning they may recompute whenever the component re-renders. Memo hooks can reduce recomputation but rely on dependency arrays.

differences.title: 7. EFFECT LIFECYCLE & CONSISTENCY
differences.leftDesc: Solid’s effects track reactive reads and rerun when dependencies change, with cleanup support. The effect graph is part of the reactive system rather than tied primarily to lifecycle phases.
differences.rightDesc: React effects are lifecycle-based: useEffect runs after paint, while useLayoutEffect runs before paint. Dependency arrays decide when effects re-run, coordinated with commit phases.
